parts.title: Listening Part 3
parts.instructions: You will hear Ethan and his mum talking about his birthday party. How will each person travel to the party? For each question, write a letter (A–H).

script.speaker: Ethan
script.text: I'm home!

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Hi, Ethan! I'm in the kitchen. Happy Birthday!

script.speaker: Ethan
script.text: Thanks, Mum! But where is everybody? Why are they so late for my party?

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Well, your sister has football practice until 6.00 p.m. Then <u>she's coming home by bus</u>.

script.speaker: Ethan
script.text: Why doesn't she take the tram? It's faster. And where's Dad?

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: He phoned to say Grandma missed the half past five bus so <u>he's going to drive her</u>.

script.speaker: Ethan
script.text: Is Granddad coming in Dad's car, too?

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: He had to work this afternoon so <u>he's going to take the underground</u>. It's quicker than the car, anyway.

script.speaker: Ethan
script.text: I can hear a motorbike. Is that Uncle Tom?

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: I spoke to him this morning. <u>He's going to take a taxi</u> after his meeting.

script.speaker: Ethan
script.text: Is Ursula coming with him? Or is she taking the underground?

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: <u>Your cousin Ursula's cycling here</u> right now. She'll be here in ten minutes.

script.speaker: Ethan
script.text: Great! Who else is coming?

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Your Aunt May!

script.speaker: Ethan
script.text: Oh. She'll come by train, won't she?

script.speaker: Mum
script.text: Actually, <u>there's a tram where she lives now, so she's getting that</u>. It's nearer than the train.

parts.title: Reading & Writing Part 3
parts.instructions: Read the text about a new type of transport. For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.passage:
A new type of transport

Alexis Lewis is a teenager from the USA. She likes to invent – to think of new ideas for things that no one has made before, and then make them.

Alexis often enters competitions for young inventors. When she was younger she spent time with her grandfather, who made transport for people to go to space. One day Alexis' mother told her about a newspaper article which explained how difficult it was to get sick people through the countryside to hospital in Africa. Alexis wanted to help.

Alexis knew that in North America, before there were cars, horses pulled heavy things on a travois (a type of sledge), made of wood. Alexis thought people could do the same, but she added wheels. To make her travois light, she used bamboo, a plant which grows in Africa, not wood.

To pull Alexis' travois, you wear a belt, which means you can carry or hold other things. Alexis thinks her travois might be useful for carrying food home from the market, as well as taking people to hospital. Now it's finished, she's writing instructions for building one so people in Africa can make it themselves.

With help from US companies, Alexis plans to give ten travois free to hospitals in Africa. She doesn't want money for them because they are for poor people.

Alexis doesn't know if she wants to be an inventor when she's older, because she also likes music and writing, but she thinks it's important for children to learn about inventing at school.

items.question: Why did Alexis decide to invent a new type of transport?
options: She wanted to win a competition.
Her mother told her about a problem.
Her grandfather worked on spaceships.

items.question: How is Alexis' travois different from those pulled by horses?
options: It is heavier.
It is made of wood.
It has wheels.

items.question: What does the writer say about using Alexis' travois?
options: People will need instructions to use it.
People should not use it to carry shopping.
People can pull it without using their hands.

items.question: What does the writer say about Alexis' future?
options: She might do something different from inventing.
She would like to teach children how to invent.
She hopes she can start to sell her inventions.

items.question: What is the writer doing in this text?
options: advertising a new way to travel
telling the story of someone's idea
asking for help with a problem

parts.title: Reading & Writing Part 3
parts.instructions: Read the text about a lorry driver. For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.passage:
The lorry driver

My aunt Naomi is a lorry driver. When she left school she didn't know what she wanted to do, so she went to work in a supermarket. One day, she was talking to one of the lorry drivers at the supermarket, and she decided she wanted to drive a lorry herself. She went home and told her parents (my grandparents!), and they thought it was a good idea.

Naomi's journeys are different every day, and she goes to every part of the country. She enjoys the driving, but she says that one day, she would like to get a job with a different company so she can drive to other countries. Lots of other drivers do this.

Naomi says she likes being out on the road, seeing new towns all the time, but the best thing about driving lorries for her is chatting to everyone she sees during her working day. She also says the lorries are really comfortable, so she doesn't mind sleeping in them. For her, they are her home on wheels!

I asked my grandparents what they thought about Naomi's job. They are happy that Naomi's happy, so they don't want her to change jobs. But they worry about her because it's sometimes a dangerous job and she spends a lot of time away from home.

items.question: Where did Naomi get the idea to be a lorry driver?
options: at school
at work
at home

items.question: What does the second paragraph tell us about Naomi's job?
options: She drives all around the world.
She often drives to the same places.
She hopes to work for another company in the future.

items.question: What does Naomi like most about her job?
options: the travelling
the people
the lorries

items.question: What do Naomi's parents think about her job?
options: They would like Naomi to do a different job.
They are glad it's such an exciting job.
They believe the job has some problems.

items.question: What is the writer doing in the text?
options: explaining how to get one type of work
describing someone's work
giving advice about doing difficult work

parts.title: Listening Part 5
parts.instructions: You will hear Marcia talking to her friend Josh about taking the school bus. Where does each person catch the school bus? For each question, write a letter (A–H).

script.speaker: Marcia
script.text: I'm going to start taking the school bus next week, Josh. Where should I catch it?

script.speaker: Josh
script.text: Well, I catch it from Hill Street. After the railway bridge, there's a <u>roundabout</u>, and my bus stop's there.

script.speaker: Marcia
script.text: OK. Does Max catch it there? He lives near you.

script.speaker: Josh
script.text: No. His mum drives him into town because she works at the motorbike shop. She leaves her car in the <u>car park</u> in George Street. Max catches the bus there.

script.speaker: Josh
script.text: Oliver gets on at the bus stop in New Street, by the <u>bridge</u> – not the one near the cinema, the other one.

script.speaker: Marcia
script.text: Oh yes. I can catch it there, too. Who else goes on the bus?

script.speaker: Josh
script.text: Emily. She lives opposite the <u>cinema</u>, so she catches the bus there, not far from the tram stop.

script.speaker: Marcia
script.text: What about Katy, Emily's neighbour?

script.speaker: Josh
script.text: She doesn't like crossing the busy road, so she gets on the school bus next to the <u>traffic lights</u> behind the station.

script.speaker: Josh
script.text: Tom gets the bus too, at the <u>crossing</u>, near the supermarket.
